title: Calibrate skew-pair thresholds against sparse and high-frequency controls
statement: Using three separate works from the prior directional-pair pilot (the Vulgate Daniel, Villani and Walther), take the first 5,000 normalized words, remove one most frequent type and compare 99 within-block shuffles. Count unequal pairs at distances 1–3, call an unordered type skewed if the absolute directional count difference exceeds five, and divide by observed unordered pair types. Under both compressing removed tokens and treating them as barriers, all three originals exceed every shuffle (plus-one p=.01). The two gap policies give different denominators and scores; for Latin they count 10,189 versus 8,126 pair types. After filtering, distinct-type shares are .356/.323/.305 and singleton-type shares .223/.204/.188. As a non-language positive control, ten books of a five-token periodic cycle with randomized block phases yield zero rejections under either gap policy; the uncorrected skew fraction is often near one even under shuffling. Thirty iid five-token books also give zero rejections under each policy. The small control count means the two-sided 95% Wilson upper bounds for a zero rate are about 27.8% and 11.4%, respectively. These are diagnostic examples, not estimated general power or evidence that language alone produces the historical result.
check: Prespecify a candidate measure, tie rule, gap behavior, token and independent-block boundaries, and all thresholds before using untouched historical corpora or manuscript evaluation pages. In particular calibrate the fixed count threshold under highly frequent and sparse vocabularies, multiple nonlanguage transition processes, equal-frequency stopword ties, deterministic substitutions, noisy and planted ciphers, and clustered page nulls. A significance result relative to random word shuffles only indicates nonexchangeable local order under that null. Build and review a declarative scorer primitive only after its finite-sample and vocabulary dependence is characterized; keep distinct type counts, singleton counts and occurrence denominators separately named.

method.pairing: Within each original roughly 400-character normalized block, consider unequal forward pairs at distances 1–3. In compress mode remove stopwords before measuring distances; in barrier mode a removed token terminates the local window. Pairs never cross block boundaries. Remove the most frequent type, breaking equal frequency ties lexicographically and holding it fixed across shuffled replicates. This tie rule can break substitution invariance at a frequency tie.
method.null: Shuffle words independently inside each source block 99 times and compute plus-one one-sided tail for the same fixed stopword; no across-block moves. Periodic controls use 80-token blocks of a five-word cycle with random phases, and iid controls use the same block sizes and vocabulary. The five-word period is smaller than the natural vocabularies and is an adversarial saturation example, not a model of any manuscript.
method.selection: Source works differ from the three prior directional pilot works but were used in other project calculations; first 5,000 words are not randomly chosen. Plan file was written before the first run, then the tie rule and barrier implementation were corrected after inspecting initial outputs. Treat all results as exploratory, not an untouched preregistration.
method.limits: Only three historical works, 10 cycles and 30 iid samples; 99 random shuffles each. No manuscript outcomes, independent witnesses, historical cipher controls, reviewed scorer metric or calibrated production threshold. Original work extraction and editorial-cleaning caveats are in P-J-011.

plan.boundary: independent pre-existing normalizer blocks; never count across blocks
plan.stop_tie: lexicographic token order, fixed for each observed sequence and its permutations
plan.compare: two stopword policies: compress filtered tokens versus original-position barriers
plan.synthetic: stationary ordered five-token cycle with random phase per block; count-preserving within-block shuffle
plan.negative: 30 iid uniform five-token books; same 80-token blocks

reproduction.instruction: Reconstruct clean_works.json by extracting extract_works.py from P-J-011/mubadala777/step.json and running it with pinned project inputs. Save the included plan and script in /tmp using the named paths, and run the script; edit paths if another scratch directory is used.
